en: The Hymn to Āditya Endowed with Great Majesty.
Now begins the Ādityastotra, endowed with great majesty, composed by the illustrious Appayya Dīkṣita.
Measuring ten thousand *yojanas* in breadth and length, it is established upon a wheel possessing five spokes, three hubs, and six shining rims;
its yoke is borne by seven horses representing the meters, and it traverses the three divisions of time.
May the chariot of the fierce-rayed sun, with all its parts clearly fashioned, manifest before me. || 1 ||
Surrounded by the Ādityas, Apsarases, sages, lords of serpents, Grāmaṇīs, Yātudhānas,
Gandharvas, and Vālakhilyas, he occupied the center of the entire solar chariot,
pervading its middle like a jewel within the orb of the fierce-rayed sun in the sky.
The manifestation of the light of Brahman, whose form is the condensed essence of the multitude of Vedas, blazes forth.

Emerging from the solar orb, these channels— originating from all living beings and entering the heart-channel of that Sun, who is like honey to the hosts of gods such as the Vasus— issue forth from various directions,
raining down warm water and even snow while drinking up waters on all sides.
The sprouts of splendor belonging to the ancestors and others shine forth, produced by the essence of the nectar of the *svadhā* oblation. || 3 ||
Among those who pervade the five directions, you are the most excellent in a thousand; illuminating the moon, the host of stars, and the five beginning with Mercury—
the moon, the sun, and the rest— you become the seven suns at the conflagration of the three worlds, O Bhrāja and your brothers.
May Suṣumnā and the others here dispel all my diseases with the rays of the Sun. || 4 ||
Sixty-nine thousand other rays, endowed with [sixty-nine] qualities, depend upon the Ādityas;
divided month by month, they shine forth, purifying the abode of the three worlds.
When those rays that protect the world rise from the seven [principal] rays and cease to move upon the earth—
During a *saṃsarpa* year and an intercalary month, virtuous rites such as vows and sacrifices are not performed.
The Sun, whose body shines crimson within his orb, who pervades the universe with his splendor,
and who is served by the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas through the division of morning, midday, and evening;
he is both the goal to be attained and the attainer himself, renowned in the northern path of those possessing supreme knowledge.
I take refuge in that which is to be meditated upon as the manifest Brahman itself, which arises as the remover of all fears.
The entire regulated authority over their respective months, such as the emitting of heat, snow, and water upon the earth, belongs to the suns presided over by His power;
for the Blessed Lord Himself, manifesting as the twelve among them, reveals that preeminence.
Bow down to him, the root of the three worlds, the supreme deity, the one with seven horses (the Sun).
The celestial nymphs, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, the best of sages, serpents, and Rākṣasas—

these twelve groups of twelve, with their vast retinues, constantly spread joy for him by means of dances, songs, the offering of oblations, the propitiation of the planets, and service performed before him.
I worship that Friend of the World with heart-pleasing verses spoken by the Vālakhilyas. || 8 ||

I behold that Truth, the eternal Brahman, whose birth in the cosmic egg at dawn was proclaimed by the foremost sons of the Supreme Brahman, who is the object of meditation through the three *vyāhṛtis* beginning with the head, the arms, and the feet; I behold Him daily as the one named *Aham*, whose form is the Sun.
Of all beings dwelling in the elements, from the earth up to the sky, [he is] that single subtle portion of life-force.
To the yogis whose minds are focused upon the Sun, the eye of the world,
he appears within as a form with the luster of pure gold, possessing a pair of eyes as expansive as blossoming lotuses,
with the *Ṛg* and *Sāman* verses as his neck-ornaments, and the nature of the unsurpassed, shimmering Lord of the World’s desires.
I take refuge in Śambhu, the Brahman who is both arisen and fully risen, because all faults have been cast off. || 10 ||
May the worship of that syllable *Om*— which has attained the status of being a constituent part of the *Udgītha* chant and which resides within the solar orb— remove all evil;
for even the *kṛcchra* penances, though primarily intended for ritual worship, destroy every sin when directed toward it.
May this primordial Supreme Śiva, the physician, who has been meditated upon, remove all our afflictions. 11.

I take constant refuge in Śiva, the blue-throated, three-eyed, whose form is the universe, who is served by the Gāyatrī mantra, who impels the intellects of all beings, and who shines with a light reaching the path of the eyes of everyone from cowherds and women to the sun itself— blazing within the solar orb as the Person through the penetration of its beginning, end, and middle. 12.
The cloud-like kalpas, the hundred-limbed [Manvantaras], the circle consisting of stable gold, and the thousands of rays—
among these, seven are declared by the Vedas, as well as slightly less than a hundred thousand;
then for each of the sun, the primordial deity, there are four, and subsequently three.
These twelve *sragdharā* verses have been composed, honored for their manifestation of various specific powers. || 13 ||
It shakes off bad dreams, ill omens, all misfortunes, even incurable diseases, the defects arising from malefic planetary positions, and evil spirits such as Grahas;
it bestows stable prosperity in this world, and one attains liberation at the end.
Having recited this jewel of a hymn even once daily for the Lord of Days, a person—
Thus ends the *Śrīmad-Āditya-stotra-ratna* composed by the illustrious Appayya Dīkṣita.
